source_text: V. Iratus itaque Probus super fiduciam beatissimi viri, iussit eum etiam gladio percuti. sanctus vero dei martyr, tamquam secundam palmam accipiens, deo gratias agebat dicens: Tibi gratias ago, domine Iesu Christe, qui mihi per varias poenas et tormenta donas tolerantiam et aeternae gloriae me participem efficere dignatus es. et cum venisset ad pontem qui vocatur Basentis, exspolians se vestimenta sua et extendens manus in caelum oravit dicens: Domine Iesu Christe, qui pro mundi salute pati dignatus es, pateant caeli tui, ut suscipiant angeli spiritum servi tui Irenaei, qui propter nomen tuum et plebem tuam productam de ecclesia tua catholica Sirmiensium haec patior. te peto, tuamque deprecor misericordiam, ut et me suscipere et hos in fide tua confirmare digneris. sic itaque percussus gladio a ministris proiectus est in fluvium Savi. VI. Martyrizatus est famulus dei sanctus Irenaeus episcopus civitatis Sirmiensium die VIII. idus Aprilis sub Diocletiano imperatore, agente Probo praeside, regnante domino nostro Iesu Christo; cui est gloria in saecula saeculorum, amen.
orientation: After Probus sentences Irenaeus to drowning and Irenaeus asks for the sword as well, Probus orders it and Irenaeus is led to the bridge over the Sava.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore Probus having become angry over the confidence of the most blessed man ordered him to be struck also with the sword. But the holy martyr of God as receiving a second palm was giving thanks to God saying: I give thanks to you Lord Jesus Christ who through various punishments and torture give to me endurance and have deemed worthy to make me a sharer of eternal glory. And when he had come to the bridge which is called Basentis stripping off his own clothes and stretching out his hands into heaven he prayed saying: Lord Jesus Christ who for the salvation of the world have deemed worthy to suffer let your heavens lie open in order that the angels may receive the spirit of your servant Irenaeus who on account of your name and your people brought forth from your church of Sirmium suffer these things. I ask you and I entreat your mercy in order that you may deem worthy both to receive me and to strengthen these men in your faith. So thus having been struck with the sword by the attendants he was thrown into the river Sava. The holy servant of God Irenaeus bishop of the city of Sirmium was martyred on the eighth day before the Ides of April under Diocletian as emperor with Probus acting as governor with our Lord Jesus Christ reigning to whom is glory into ages of ages amen.

pass_b_english: Probus, angered by the confidence of the blessed man, ordered him to be struck also with the sword. Receiving it as a second palm, God's holy martyr gave thanks to God. Irenaeus says, "I give you thanks, Lord Jesus Christ, for through many punishments and torture you give me endurance and have graced me to share in eternal glory."

When he came to the bridge called Basentis, he stripped off his clothes and stretched his hands toward heaven and prayed. Irenaeus says, "Lord Jesus Christ, you were willing to suffer for the salvation of the world. Let your heavens stand open, so that angels may receive the spirit of your servant Irenaeus. I suffer this for your name and for your people, brought forth from your church of Sirmium. I ask you and entreat your mercy to receive me and to strengthen these in your faith."

Then the attendants struck him with the sword and threw him into the Sava River. God's holy servant Irenaeus, bishop of the city of Sirmium, was martyred on April 6 under the emperor Diocletian, when Probus was governor, while our Lord Jesus Christ reigns, to whom is glory forever and ever, amen.
